misclassified_entities.reason: Internal component - eth/les subprotocols are part of the node's internal message handling, not an external entity
Internal component - TCP socket interface is internal to node; the external entity is the peer, not the socket

trusted_external_entities.name: Transaction Sender (EIP-158)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External account submitting transactions that trigger account touches. Transactions may intentionally create or touch empty accounts during transition period.

trusted_external_entities.name: State Churn Attacker
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Malicious actor exploiting cheap state modifications during EIP-158 transition. Can perform ~700 gas touches to empty accounts to increase state churn and uncle rates.

trusted_external_entities.name: JSON-RPC Client (Block/Uncle Queries)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: External application querying block data via eth_getBlockByHash or eth_getUncleByBlockNumberAndIndex. May probe for fork status or submit malformed requests.

trusted_external_entities.name: Decentralized Application (Chain Switch)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Web application requesting wallet_switchEthereumChain. Could be legitimate or attempting to trick user into switching to malicious chain. User consent required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Potentially Malicious Dapp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Dapp that may probe wallet capabilities via chain switch requests for fingerprinting, or attempt social engineering to switch user to attacker-controlled chain.

trusted_external_entities.name: DEVp2p Peer Node
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote Ethereum node connecting via DEVp2p. Protocol version negotiation required. May be malicious, attempting to downgrade to v4 or send malformed compressed data.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious DEVp2p Peer
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Attacker attempting compression-based DoS attacks via decompression bombs, varint overflow, or malformed Snappy streams. All compressed data must be validated before decompression.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Transaction operations may touch accounts for emptiness evaluation. Zero-value operations no longer charge 25k gas for account creation post-EIP-158.
Attack window limited to transition period. Empty accounts will eventually be cleared. Network must tolerate increased uncle rates during clearing.
Request parameters validated. baseFee field included only for post-EIP-1559 blocks. Pre-1559 blocks must not include baseFee. Null returned for missing blocks.
Uncle block queries validated against fork block. baseFee correctly included/omitted based on EIP-1559 activation status. Fork configuration must be accurate.
User confirmation required before switching. Requester identity and target chain displayed to user. Pending RPC requests cancelled on switch.
Privacy risk: automatic rejection may reveal wallet chain support. Fingerprinting countermeasures needed. Clear requester identification to user.
Version negotiation determines compression mode. v4 = no compression, v5+ = Snappy compression. Cannot trust peer version claims until handshake complete.
Varint size check (≤2^32-1) and 16MB decompression limit checked BEFORE decompression. Decompression bombs rejected. Message rejection on any validation failure.
